Subject: MAP: performance metrics correlation and triage plan

Hi Jules —

Thanks again for the time on Wednesday. As discussed, I attached an updated mutual action plan (acme_map_v2.xlsx) that folds in the performance evaluation work we committed to: latency/TTFT sampling across sequence lengths, throughput at target concurrency, and an initial comparison versus the competitive baseline you provided.

Key asks from Redwood (what we'll deliver):
- A reproducible eval harness (we'll hand over our runner + config) and a short patch to match your request routing patterns.
- A concise results sheet with TTFT/median P50/P95, tokens/sec, and concurrency curves for the top two model candidates.
- A suggested rollout and fallback policy for the initial pilot to stay within your latency SLOs.

Key asks from Acme (what we need from you):
- A small representative prompt set (20–50 sequences) and the typical sequence length distribution (percentiles).
- Confirmation of the environment we should reproduce on (your staging cluster details or a managed snapshot).
- Access to the competitor run file you referenced so we can align methodology.

I've put tentative owners and due dates in the MAP. Proposed timeline: reproduce -> align on methodology -> run head-to-head on identical harness -> deliver results and recommended config by 2027-09-21 so you have time for procurement before EOW.

Notes on methodology we want to align on (high-level):
- Warm vs cold KV cache (hot-path caching can materially change TTFT for chat workloads).
- How you count TTFT (first-token vs total latency for the request).
- Input tokenization/prefix padding and batching window.
- Failure injection and tail-case retries.

I'll schedule a 30-min working session next week to agree the alignment matrix and hand off the harness. Happy to shift timelines if your procurement cadence is different.

Ben

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: MAP: performance metrics correlation and triage plan

Ben—quick internal note before we lock the session with Acme.

Observed differences in recent MAP repros that we should call out explicitly so the customer knows what to expect: 
- Runner differences: our default harness uses a micro-batching window (20ms) and an adaptive KV warm-up; many customers use JMeter-style clients that do no warming and pad to max length. That changes both median TTFT and throughput curves.
- Sequence sampling: "representative set" needs explicit percentiles (p50/p90/p99) and percent long-tail requests. If their set skews long we should propose a split run.
- Competitive baseline: some vendors report steady-state tokens/sec after long warm-up — not TTFT. We need to normalize to first-response latency when the customer cares about UX.

Action items for us before the call:
1) Prepare the eval harness patch that toggles warming behavior and batching window (owner: Karthik, due: 2027-09-13).
2) Draft a short one-pager describing the metrics (TTFT-first-token vs request-latency, tokens/sec, P95 tail). I'll include that in the Drive folder (owner: Marissa, due: 2027-09-12).

Adding both to the MAP and marking as internal risks for the sales close.

—Marissa

Thanks Ben — we downloaded the MAP and ran an initial pass over our staging environment with the competitor harness. Attaching our condensed run (perf_run_20270912.csv). A few observations from our side: 

- Your baseline numbers look directionally right but we see ~20–25% lower throughput at 8-concurrency on our staging nodes when using our JMeter clients.
- Notably, their TTFT numbers report "response-start" which is similar to your first-token metric; however they warmed the model for 30 minutes before recording. We did not warm.
- Our staging cluster has slightly different NIC settings (LRO disabled) and we have an internal proxy that batches small requests. Those two items could explain the delta.

We can do a focused repro of your harness if you share the runner and a small seed of our prompt set (we'll redact PII). Two asks from us:
1) Can Redwood provide the harness patch today (the one that lets us toggle warm vs cold)?
2) Can you confirm what startup noise we should expect (we saw a P99 spike during first ten minutes that flattened afterward)?

If we can get a short working session this week and a mutual reproduction, we can keep the Q3 procurement target. Suggested time: Wed 09/15 10:00–10:30 PT.

Thanks — Jules

Proposed mutual action items / timeline (small, commit-focused so procurement can proceed):

- 2027-09-16 EOD: Redwood delivers normalized results spreadsheet and an addendum to the MAP with recommended batching and fallback policies (owner: Marissa).
- 2027-09-18: Final alignment on rollout config + approval for pilot capacity (you sign off in the MAP).

Triage checklist we will cover during the reproduce session:
- Confirm whether NIC/proxy batching explains the tokens/sec gap.
- Confirm KV cache warm-up delta effect on P50/P95/TTFT-first-token.
- Capture traces for any P99 outliers (we'll provide a lightweight tracing snippet to drop into your staging).

If you confirm the Wed slot we'll send a calendar invite and a short runbook. We're aiming to get you a normalized sheet by 9/16 so procurement can move this week.
